newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end higher, well-supported.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end higher, well-supported.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei stock index futures ended higher on Wednesday after several attempts to break its key psychological support level of 20,000 failed, dealers said.
"SIMEX tested several support levels throughout the day. It broke the key 20,000 support briefly but quickly rebounded," a dealer with a U.S. house said.
Dealers said heavy selling of securities houses stocks in the Tokyo stock market on fears of more trading illegalities pressured SIMEX September Nikkei futures to a low of 19,980.
September found good support at 20,000 and ended at 20,210, up 70 points from Tuesday's close.
Dealers said Thailand's decision to change its exchange rate system to a managed float did not affect the Nikkei except indirectly through its impact on dollar/yen.
The news that the baht would be valued by market forces triggered selling of the dollar against the yen.
"We will sell on Thursday if SIMEX Nikkei nears 20,300 but will cover shorts if it hits 20,400," the dealer said.
All eyes remained on the two day Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meet which ends on Wednesday.
The key July Taiwan MSCI index rose 0.4 points to end at 385.0 in moderately active volume of 671 lots.
